hints.title: Root Location in Postorder Obstacle
hints.text: In postorder traversal, the root node appears at the very end of the sequence. How can locating this root element within inorder reveal which elements belong to the right versus left subtrees?

hints.title: Reverse Postorder Invariant
hints.text: The last element of postorder is the subtree root. Finding its position in inorder divides the remaining nodes into left and right subtrees of known sizes.

hints.title: Right-First Recursion Procedure
hints.text: Create a value-to-index lookup for inorder. Pop roots from the end of postorder. Because roots are popped in reverse postorder, construct the right subtree first, then the left subtree, bounded by inorder ranges.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

complexity.notes: Hash map provides O(1) lookup to partition subtrees, constructing nodes in reverse postorder.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Searching inorder linearly on each recursion degrades time complexity to quadratic O(N^2).
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: O(N) memory for the hash map to eliminate repeated linear scans.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Building the right child before the left child when popping from the end of postorder.
